## Objective
In Español, the note body, typed-notes box, refine composer and patient-name
field use a Mexican Spanish dictionary with the same features as English.

The English behaviour is unchanged and proved so (V1(a)); Spanish is lazy —
its dictionary is fetched only when a spell surface is mounted in Español
(V3), and a load failure shows an error while leaving typing usable (V1(e)).

## Fixed decisions

### D1 — NFC tokenisation that leaves English provably unchanged
`web/src/lib/spelling.ts:27` is `const WORD = /[A-Za-z]+(?:['’][A-Za-z]+)*/g`
and `plainWord` (`:37-39`) only folds `’` to `'`. The replacement:

```ts
/**
 * A word: English letters plus the Spanish ones the es-MX dictionary needs,
 * and any combining marks a keyboard or an IME may leave attached — so a word
 * typed as `sesio` + U+0301 is one token, not two.
 *
 * The ASCII letter range comes first and is unchanged, so for text carrying
 * no Spanish letter and no combining mark (U+0300–U+036F) this pattern
 * matches exactly what the old one matched, and `plainWord` is a no-op on such
 * text: English tokenisation is provably unchanged. The precondition is those
 * two classes, not the word "ASCII": the combining-mark range below is admitted
 * too, and `'` and `’` are inside the pattern in both versions.
 */
const LETTER = '[A-Za-zÁÉÍÓÚÜÑáéíóúüñ\\u0300-\\u036f]';
const WORD = new RegExp(`${LETTER}+(?:['’]${LETTER}+)*`, 'g');
```

```ts
function plainWord(word: string): string {
  // NFC first, so a decomposed `sesión` and a precomposed one are the same
  // word; then the curly apostrophe, which is not part of any word.
  return word.normalize('NFC').replace(/’/g, "'");
}
```

Five properties the card states, because each is a way this could go wrong:
- **Normalisation is per matched word, never on the whole text.**
  `Misspelling` carries `[start, end)` offsets into the **original** text
  (`spelling.ts:19-24`) and they drive the caret and the menu
  (`replaceRange`, `:59-61`; `misspellingAt`, `:55-57`). NFC applied to the
  whole text would change the length of a decomposed string and shift every
  offset after it. `Misspelling.word` stays the **raw matched substring**
  (unchanged from `spelling.ts:49`), the speller is asked with
  `plainWord(word)`, and the **original text is never normalised** — so
  `original.slice(m.start, m.end) === m.word` and
  `m.end - m.start === m.word.length` are true of every word in both
  encodings, and V1(c) compares the **cross-input projection**
  `{plainWord(m.word)}`, never the raw `m.word`.
- **No accent folding, ever.** `ñ` stays `ñ`; there is no `NFD`, no
  diacritic-stripping, no transliteration. V1(c) asserts a decomposed and a
  precomposed input give the **same NFC-normalised words** and the same
  flagged set; § *Words* asserts accented words are not flagged at all.
- **`¿` and `¡` are not letters.** They are outside the class, so a word after
  them is matched whole.
- **The allow-list gets the same treatment for free**, because `allowedWords`
  calls the same `WORD` and the same `plainWord` — so a typed `José` matches
  an allow-listed `José Ramírez` instead of `Jos` matching `jos`.
- **The suggestion alphabet is deliberately left alone**
  (`spelling.ts:123`, `LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'"`). Widening it
  would change English suggestions; an accent-only correction comes from
  `nspell`'s own suggester, and V2's non-empty-menu assertion tests it. This
  is the status quo and needs no authority.

### D3 — storage shape and the read rule
Settings is a flat key → JSON-value store (`shared/src/settings.ts:6-18`),
keys match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/`, so a key cannot be spelled `es-MX`. Two
keys: `en` keeps `spelling_words` (unchanged, `shared/src/spelling.ts:16`);
`es-MX` gets `spelling_words_es_mx` (new), a JSON array of strings.

1. The active list is chosen by the **active UI language** (`language`
   setting), not by a note's locale and not by the text in the field.
2. `en` reads `spelling_words`. `es-MX` reads `spelling_words_es_mx`; an
   absent or malformed value reads as `[]` with no new code —
   `spellingWordsFrom` (`shared/src/spelling.ts:22-31`) already reads
   defensively and is reused as-is.
3. **A Spanish list is never seeded from the English list.** The two are
   independent.
4. `stt_vocabulary` (`shared/src/transcribe.ts:99`) is **not** part of this
   change; it stays applied in both languages.
5. `MAX_SPELLING_WORDS = 1000` and `MAX_SPELLING_WORD_CHARS = 60` keep their
   values and now apply **per key**, i.e. per locale.
6. **No stored value is rewritten. There is no migration.** No backfill, no
   delete, no schema change, no new file in `server/migrations/`. `PUT
   /api/settings` merges (`shared/src/settings.ts:21`), so writing the Spanish
   key cannot clobber the English one. *The existing English list migrates
   unchanged to `en`* means *it is read as `en`'s list and is never moved,
   converted or rewritten*, **not** *a migration runs*.

**The race guarantee.** A word list is selected by the language at the moment
the settings snapshot arrives, and the provider keeps one `added` list. On a
language change the provider swaps the active key **before** the dictionary
load starts and clears the previous locale's list, so a stale snapshot cannot
repopulate the wrong language's list after the switch. The word-list half is a
case of its own (V1(i)), not a consequence of the speller one.

### D4 — the dictionary-load error surface
Today `SpellingProvider.tsx:79-81` swallows the failure on purpose and the
`Spelling` interface (`:21-31`) has no error field.

1. **State, and its type.** `Spelling` gains
   `readonly error: MessageKey | null;` — `MessageKey` is `keyof typeof en`
   (`shared/src/i18n/t.ts:50`), already exported at `shared/src/index.ts:566`.
   Typing the field as the key union makes a typo a `npm run typecheck`
   failure. It is set when a locale's load rejects, cleared on the next
   successful load, and reset to `null` on a language change **before** the
   new load starts. `INERT` (`:33-38`) gains `error: null`.
2. **Behaviour while failed is exactly today's**, not a degraded mode:
   `speller` stays `null`, no marks are drawn, `findMisspellings` is never
   called, `addWord`/`ignoreWord` still work, typing is untouched.
   **The no-retry fact, stated so it is not "fixed" by accident:**
   `ensureLoaded` sets `loadingRef.current = true` and clears it nowhere
   (`SpellingProvider.tsx:72-82`), so a failed load is never retried for the
   life of the tab. Making it retryable is out of scope here.
3. **The race guard is new code, and the card says so.** The provider has
   only `mountedRef` today; there is **no** request id. The guard is a
   monotonic counter incremented on every load start and every language
   change; a resolved load installs its speller and clears `error` only if its
   own id is still current. V1(f) asserts both directions.
4. **Surface.** `web/src/components/SpellLayer.tsx` renders one line per
   **mounted** spell surface, in the editor's own wrap, with `role="alert"`,
   using `t('spelling.loadFailed')`. It is rendered by the shared spell layer,
   not the menu. It is **one alert per mounted spell surface, not "one line,
   once"**: `SpellLayer` is mounted once per field (`ChatComposer.tsx:60`,
   `NoteBody.tsx:137`, `PatientRenameField.tsx:72`, `web/src/routes/AddPatient.tsx:114`,
   `Capture.tsx:447`), so a note page with the chat open renders it twice.

#### The message (coordinator §12 item 1 — routine catalogue copy)

| Catalogue | Key | Text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shared/src/i18n/en.ts` | `spelling.loadFailed` | `Spell check is unavailable` |
| `shared/src/i18n/es-MX.ts` | `spelling.loadFailed` | `La corrección ortográfica no está disponible` |

Grounding, so this is a derivation and not an invention:
- English is one clause in the register of the adjacent block
  (`spelling.none` = "No suggestions", `spelling.ignore` = "Ignore",
  `spelling.add` = "Add to dictionary") and of the existing one-clause
  failure lines (`workspace.serverUnreachable` = "Apunta can’t reach its
  server"; `note.saveError` = "Couldn’t save").
- The Spanish reuses the block's own head noun — `spelling.menuLabel` is
  already `Ortografía de {word}` — and the catalogue's construction for "not
  available": `errors.language_unavailable` reads *"El español no está
  disponible en esta versión de Apunta. Elige inglés o instala la edición en
  español."* (two clauses, unlike this one).
- **No trailing full stop**, matching the one-clause alert style.
- The key takes **no placeholder**. Adding it to one catalogue and not the
  other fails `shared/src/i18n/t.test.ts`'s parity rule (`:568-589`); a
  literal in the component fails `scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs`, which
  `npm run lint` runs.
- The Spanish value must not leak English: V2's `checkScreen` reads it in the
  `es-MX` project through `expectNoEnglishUi`, unchanged.

### D6 — locale-specific spec selection, and the coverage it keeps
`e2e/playwright.config.ts:107-113` re-runs every spec except
`language-control.spec.ts` in the `es-MX` project, against a server started
with `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1`, whose data folder leaves the stored `language` at
`es-MX`. `e2e/tests/spelling.spec.ts:46` asserts exactly
`['Teh', 'criticised']` against whatever dictionary is loaded. Once D3 ties
the dictionary to the active UI language, the `es-MX` project loads Spanish
and every English assertion there is evaluated against Spanish. Separately,
the `chromium` project (`:100`) has **no** `testIgnore` and would collect the
new Spanish spec against a build that does not offer Spanish.

Suppressing the English spec in the `es-MX` project is **not** suppressing a
failing applicable test: under D3 an English-dictionary assertion in a project
whose UI language is `es-MX` is not applicable by construction. The exact
config change — **two entries, one per project, nothing else**:

```ts
projects: [
  { name: 'chromium', testIgnore: /spelling-es\.spec\.ts$/, use: { ... } },
  // es-MX-language: unchanged
  { name: 'es-MX', testIgnore: [/language-control/, /spelling\.spec\.ts$/], use: { ... } },
]
```

Neither spec name appears in a **global** `testIgnore`. **Neither entry names
`e2e/tests/spelling-assets.spec.ts`:** that file holds the dictionary-asset
laziness/reachability case alone, is project-agnostic, and is **collected by
both** the `es-MX` and the `chromium` project; V3 runs it in `es-MX` and V6 in
`chromium`.

**Four conditions travel with it, as card text:**
1. **Project-scoped and minimal**, exactly as above.
2. **The English coverage that is lost is named, and replaced — and what is
   *reproduced* is named apart from what is *new*.** The English spec asserts
   four things V2's Spanish expectation does not: `spellcheck="false"` on each
   surface (`:48`, `:75`, `:94`), **applying** a correction from the menu
   (`:64-69`), the caret/menu edge-click behaviour (`:51-59`, `:76-81`,
   `:95-100`), and `checkScreen` on the spelling menu (`:63`).
   `spelling.spec.ts` exercises the **note body** (`:44`), the **refine
   composer** (`:72`) and the **add-patient** name input (`:85`, at
   `/patients/new`). The **typed-notes box** (`web/src/routes/Capture.tsx:447`)
   and the patient **rename** field (`rename-field-<id>`,
   `PatientRenameField.tsx:64` mounted from `PatientsColumn.tsx:1157`) are
   **new Spanish coverage this card adds** — no English spec ever drove them —
   and the return file must say so **in those words**.
   `spelling-es.spec.ts` must reproduce **the first three on the surfaces the
   English spec actually covered**, plus `checkScreen` on the Spanish menu, and
   must additionally cover the two new surfaces. The caret case is **named,
   not left to judgement**: `setSelectionRange` at the same offset within the
   marked word as `spelling.spec.ts:52-57`, and the menu must open. A sub-case
   that proves impossible in Spanish is recorded as a loss **in those words**,
   naming the surface; it may not be dropped silently.
3. **The ignore is visible in evidence, not silent.** `testIgnore` removes a
   file from collection and Playwright does not report it as skipped, so V2's
   evidence records the **per-project collected-test counts** and the return
   file states the delta.
4. **No self-skip, and no loosening inside `spelling.spec.ts`.** No
   `test.skip()`/`skip()` inside the new spec — a spec that skips itself is a
   vacuous green, which `docs/v2/HARD-STOPS.md` and
   `e2e/support/no-english.ts:30-36` both forbid. `spelling.spec.ts` stays
   byte-identical, which V7 checks.

### D8 — the licence mechanism, the pin, the install

**A separate map; `DUAL_LICENSED_CHOICES` is not touched** (`:48` is the
permissive-arm map and MPL-1.1 is not permissive):

```js
/**
 * Data objects shipped under a non-permissive arm of a multi-licence, elected
 * by the owner and recorded in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md and docs/decisions.md.
 * Kept apart from DUAL_LICENSED_CHOICES on purpose: that map is for permissive
 * arms, and a copyleft arm described as a permissive choice would make this
 * guard say the opposite of what it is for.
 *
 * `dictionary-es-mx` — the Mexican Spanish Hunspell word list, data only
 * (`index.aff` + `index.dic`), shipped unmodified under its own names.
 */
const DATA_LICENCE_CHOICES = new Map([
  ['dictionary-es-mx', { offered: '(GPL-3.0 OR LGPL-3.0 OR MPL-1.1)', taken: 'MPL-1.1' }],
]);
```

The two call-site changes have semantics **identical** to the existing map's —
same exact-string `offered` comparison, same fail-closed default, same
rendering:
- `isForbidden(name, license)` (`:51-57`): a package is refused unless its
  entry exists in `DUAL_LICENSED_CHOICES` **or** `DATA_LICENCE_CHOICES` with
  an `offered` string **exactly equal** to the lockfile's licence string. A
  missing entry is still a refusal.
- `reportedLicense(name, license)` (`:59-66`): consult both maps.

Nothing else changes: not `FORBIDDEN` (`:35`), not the single existing `jszip`
entry, not any of the three `process.exit(1)` paths (`:140`, `:192`, `:203`).
The optional one-liner naming the second map in `isForbidden`'s refusal
message (`:137-140`) is inside May edit either way; if changed, V4's diff
expectation must name it.

**The version pin.** `web/package.json` gets `"dictionary-es-mx": "2.0.0"` —
exact, no caret — the same string `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts:74` carries and
`locales.test.ts:52-59` asserts. C-LANG@1's table
(`docs/v2/CONTRACTS.md`, **cited by content** — `:300-305` at this writing)
says *per S1.5* and does not itself fix the version. V4 asserts the three copies agree: `locales.ts`, the resolved
lockfile entry, and the installed `node_modules/dictionary-es-mx/package.json`
version. A mismatch is a `FAIL`.

**A residual, stated rather than fixed.** The exception maps are keyed by
package name with no version component (`collect-licenses.mjs:48`), so a
future bump to a different licence string would still pass on a stale
election. A version-scoped key is a **named follow-up** (§ *Named
follow-ups*), not this card's work; the `docs/decisions.md` row states the
election **at a version** and V4's one-row diff makes a bump visible.

### Notice — the four Exhibit A fields (AM-203 item 2(a))
The notice is a fixed template with four fields
(`S6.1-NOTICE-PROVENANCE.md` §3.1, §4). Field by field:

| Exhibit A field | This card's value |
| --- | --- |
| The Original Code is … | the Mexican Spanish (`es_MX`) Hunspell pair (`index.aff` + `index.dic`), as released by the RLA-ES project (`sbosio/rla-es`) and normalised/packaged by `wooorm/dictionaries`, shipped here unmodified under its own names. The descriptive half is sourced; the **scope** half (whether the normalised build is a Modification) is `[interpretation]`, S1.5 §3.7 Q1 — not answered |
| The Initial Developer of the Original Code is … | **"Santiago Bosio"** — adopted from the `Para: es_MX` AUTOR (`S6.1-NOTICE-PROVENANCE.md` §4, Source A). The project owner's name must **never** be substituted for it |
| Portions created by … are Copyright (C) … All Rights Reserved | **`[unknown]`** — no `es_MX`-specific copyright line exists upstream. Next step **U2**: a separately authorised read of an upstream `es_MX` release archive header, or an upstream maintainer statement |
| Contributor(s): … | **`[unknown]`** — whether the normalised build is a Modification is `[interpretation]`. Next step **U3**: the owner's call, on advice; if it is a Modification, the sourced names are Titus Wormer and Thomas Beverley (Source D), not the project owner |

**The notice is not yet shippable.** There are exactly two outcomes: every
field has a resolved, sourced value and the notice ships; or a field does not,
in which case the notice is **not written into the shipped file at all**. Under
AM-203 the two `[unknown]` fields are unresolved, so **nothing with a blank is
written into `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`** and **V4 is `BLOCKED`, never passed**,
until U2 and U3 are sourced (Stop 2). If a placeholder form is used in this
card's draft text, it must never reach the shipped file. The two open legal
questions of S1.5 §3.7 are recorded next to the notice in the file **only if
and when** all four fields resolve.

## Steps
Run in order, **after Stop 1 is confirmed cleared** (it is, by AM-203 item 1):

```
Step 1 (Fixed decision). Edit web/package.json: add "dictionary-es-mx": "2.0.0".
Step 2 (Fixed decision). Install it, from the repository root:
  npm install --workspace @apunta/web --save-exact --no-audit --no-fund dictionary-es-mx@2.0.0
Step 3 (Fixed decision). Record Step 2 in the checkpoint's sideEffectsDone, at
        that moment, with its exit code.
```

Why each flag: `--workspace @apunta/web` puts the data where `speller.ts`
addresses it (`new URL('../../../node_modules/…')`); `--save-exact` guarantees
the `"2.0.0"` rather than a caret; `--no-audit --no-fund` keeps the
acquisition to A11's one host, whose query-key allowance is `none`, so a query
string is refused before the URL is requested. **Integrity:** A11 requires a
digest and `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md:4-7` accepts the package manager's
integrity string. The expected registry integrity for `2.0.0` is
`sha512-EkRPJAgPhY55oMiHqwEBavOpokkvXlOO5jOdwZJmV/B6w9pGpJxlm7YorgHjiB2HqyPGW0FRcOoJRBTspTXUEA==`
(shasum `30fb094031481fff76cf0fd40bcfd9163149bc00`, S1.5 §2.2). V4 compares
the lockfile's recorded `integrity` against it byte for byte; a mismatch is a
`FAIL` and the install is reported, not re-pinned. A per-file SHA-256 of
`index.aff`/`index.dic` is optional; if not computed, the evidence records
`[not computed]` with the reason. The tarball digest is not required.

arrangement S2.10 and S2.11 already run under. **V9 is a fourth, non-browser
row:** it starts no server, opens no database and runs no test suite — it is a
`sort`/`comm`/`grep` comparison over the two files V3 and V6 already wrote, and
runs after both. **Nothing here is executed until the card is dispatched.**

**Why one `sandbox.mjs env`, and why V2/V3 may name a `--project`.**
`sandbox.mjs`'s `printEnv` exports exactly seven variables

**nor** `APUNTA_E2E_ES_DATA_DIR`. Sourcing a second env after the first moves
the **English** server onto the second port and leaves the Spanish one on a
port nothing reserved (`docs/v2/cards/S2.10.md:659-668`,

`sandbox.mjs env --port <p1>`; the Playwright config allocates the Spanish
server and its data folder itself. V3 needs **no separate build command**: the

(`e2e/playwright.config.ts:115-131`).

### Words (the concrete fabricated words)
Every word below is invented or is ordinary non-clinical Spanish vocabulary.
The V2 spec names no patient by an invented display name either: it takes its
Spanish display name from `e2e/fixtures/eval-es/NAMES.md`, so HS-8's text is
satisfied directly. `scripts/v2/check-es-fixtures.mjs` scans the two eval
corpus roots regardless, and this spec writes nothing into them.

**V1 and V2 must flag exactly these three, and nothing else in the sentence:**

| Word | Why this one |
| --- | --- |
| `brócolido` | invented; no Spanish word list contains it |
| `zambumbia` | invented; ditto |
| `telaraosa` | invented; ditto |

**V1 and V2 must not flag any of these:**

| Word | Why this one |
| --- | --- |
| `sesión` | accented, and the word the ASCII tokeniser used to cut in half |
| `atención` | accented |
| `psicología` | accented, and the locale's own stress test |
| `niño` | `ñ`, which is not an accented vowel |
| `última` | leading accent, where a naive `^[^aeiou]*` guess would fail |
| `café` | everyday, unremarkable, and the kind of word that must not become noise |
| `José`, `Ramírez` | accented, and the allow-list path of D1 |

The assertions are **exact array equality** on the flagged words and **exact
empty** on the unflagged set, so a later dictionary bump that changes an answer
fails the row instead of silently redefining it.

**Contingency, stated so it cannot be used to weaken the row:** if the shipped
`dictionary-es-mx@2.0.0` disagrees with any line of the two tables, **or with
V2's non-empty-suggestion requirement**, the row is a `FAIL`, the actual output
is quoted in the return file, and the only responses are to fix the
implementation or bring the discrepancy to the coordinator. Re-baselining the
expected arrays to whatever the dictionary says is **not** a response, and
neither is dropping a word from a table.

**V2's misspelling, and the suggestion requirement.** The e2e spec types
`nertua` (a transposition of `ternura`) and requires that clicking the mark
opens a menu with a **non-empty** suggestion list. It does **not** require a
particular suggestion: the exact strings `nspell` returns depend on the shipped
affix file. The *non-empty* requirement is the real assertion, and it also
exercises D1's unchanged ASCII `LETTERS` alphabet.

1. **The election is not on record.** Cleared by AM-203 item 1: the 2026-10-04
   `docs/decisions.md` row exists. If V0 is nevertheless red, stop, `BLOCKED`,
   and report exactly what `docs/decisions.md` does and does not say, quoted.
   Do not record the election, do not install the package, do not run V1–V4 or
   V8.
2. **Any of Exhibit A's four fields lacks a resolved, sourced value.** Under
   AM-203 the *Portions created by …* and *Contributor(s)* fields are
   `[unknown]`, so this stop **is in force — but it blocks the notice and V4
   only** (AM-203 item 2(a): the notice is unshippable, the rest of the card
   proceeds). Do not write the notice into the shipped file
   (`THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` carries **no** notice section, **no**
   `{{OWNER: …}}` placeholder and **no** blank field), record **V4 as
   `BLOCKED`, never `PASS`**, and **proceed with V0–V3 and V5–V9, recording
   each**. A notice carrying a blank never ships; every field resolved is the
   only other outcome.
3. **A file outside May edit would have to change** — stop and report the
   path. `e2e/tests/spelling.spec.ts`, `e2e/support/no-english.ts`,
   `e2e/support/fixtures.ts` and `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts` are the four most
   likely, and each is a deliberate exclusion.
4. **The predicted `npm run lint` copyleft failure appears** and the fix is not
   the D8 map — stop and report the exact `isForbidden` line. Do not widen
   `FORBIDDEN`, do not add the package to `DUAL_LICENSED_CHOICES`, and do not
   add an `ALLOWED` entry anywhere to get a row green.
5. **The lockfile `integrity` differs from S1.5 §2.2's string**, or the three
   copies of `2.0.0` disagree — `FAIL`, with both values quoted. Do not re-pin

8. **V3's or V6's positive half fails**, or **V9's difference is not exactly

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-LANG@1 Language, documents and jobs

**Built by** S2.1. **Proven by** S2.6, S4b.1, S5.6. **Consumers:** web,
server routes, AI prompts, guards, speech, spell check, formats, backup.

1. Setting `language` ∈ `en` | `es-MX`, default `en`. The server exposes
   `spanishAvailable: boolean`: true only when `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1` (D12).
   When false, the Language control is hidden and `es-MX` is rejected by
   `PUT /api/settings` with code `language_unavailable`.
2. Locale mapping (one table in `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts`):

   | App | UI and `Intl` | Whisper `-l` | Speech model | Dictionary | Prompts |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `en` | unchanged from today | `en` | `ggml-tiny.en.bin` | current English | current |
   | `es-MX` | `es-MX` | `es` | per C-STT selection | per S1.5 | Spanish set |

3. Documents: migration adds `locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'` to notes
   and to formats. **All existing rows are `en`.** New notes take the job's
   locale. Existing notes and formats are never translated or relabelled.
4. Jobs capture `{ locale, sttModel, llmModel, promptSet }` at start
   (recording, transcription, draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm).
   Retries, SSE and persistence use the captured context, never the current
   setting. **Refine uses the target note's locale**, whatever the UI
   language and whatever language the request is typed in.
5. Section roles: `shared/src/section-roles.ts` maps known section names in
   both languages (case- and accent-insensitive) to role IDs (`location`,
   `presentation`, `risk`, `discussion`, `intervention`, `actions`,
   `next_session`, and the SOAP and intake roles). Guards use roles, not
   strings. Unknown sections get role `custom`. Stored strings are not
   rewritten.
6. Changing Language is blocked while any job or save is active: the web
   control is disabled with a reason; the server also returns 409
   `language_change_blocked` if it knows of an active job.
7. Spanish dictation requires the Spanish speech model to be ready (C-ACQ).
   If it is not, dictation shows "Spanish speech model not installed" with
   a download action. **Spanish audio is never sent to the English model.**
8. The Spanish standard format is created as a separate format with
   `locale: 'es-MX'`; English formats are untouched. Imported formats take
   the UI language at import time; the user can change a format's locale.
9. Backups and restores carry the `locale` columns.
10. Treatment-plan activation writes its attestation in the stored language
    captured once at activation, because activation is not a generation job.
    Existing attestations are never rewritten or translated on read. Generated
    plan documents carry the stored value verbatim; document headings are a
    separate surface (AM-059).


**Rejection example.** UI switched to Español, user refines an existing
English note with a Spanish instruction → the note stays English, the reply
explains the change in the note's language.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
